newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks rise in late trade despite SEC move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks rise in late trade despite SEC move.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were higher in late Thursday trade, having shrugged off what brokers said was a move by the Securities and Exchange Commission to cool off the market, brokers said.
With 50 minutes left, at 0310 GMT, the index was up 50.87 points or 0.58 percent at 8,764.36, up from an intraday low of 8,647.15. Turnover was an extremely heavy T$188 billion.

The watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission said on Thursday it had reiterated rules that bar securities brokerages from forecasting market trends or recommending stock transactions in public or the media.
The move came after the Taiwan stock index surged on Wednesday to a fifth straight session, inching up to a seven-year closing high of 8,713.49 points.
Analysts said the move was aimed to cool off the market.
"Apparently, the SEC tries to cool off the rallying stock market," said Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee.
"But since sentiment is so bullish now that after a short consolidation, the index is still seen in a firming trend to test 9,000 points in the near future," Lee said.
Financials surged 2.80 percent, with China Development up T$5 to T$134.
The electronics sector, which had led recent gains, fell 1.05 percent reflecting U.S. high-tech shares' overnight losses, with leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor down T$2.5 to T$108.5.
